title: Define the business
summary: Turn an early idea or an existing business challenge into a clear audience, offer, operating model, and first delivery plan.
objective: Give the founder and delivery team a shared answer to who the company serves, which problem it solves, what it will deliver, and how the first release will be judged.
deliverables: Customer and market evidence: A research brief, ideal customer profile, buying roles, comparison map, permitted evidence sources, and documented uncertainties.
Offer and positioning: A message hierarchy, service or product packages, proposed customer journeys, and claims that can be supported by the available evidence.
Company operating blueprint: A map of acquisition, sales, fulfillment, support, and reporting responsibilities, with the first scope, dependencies, owners, and decision checkpoints.
Launch backlog: A prioritized backlog connecting each build item to a business outcome, acceptance checks, client input, and a responsible owner.

workflow.title: Understand the opportunity
workflow.description: Interview the decision makers, review existing customer evidence, define the target regions and exclusions, and identify the most important operating constraint.

workflow.title: Test the working assumptions
workflow.description: Research permitted market and account sources, retain dates and provenance, and compare the evidence with actual customer or sales feedback. AI can prepare summaries; a specialist resolves conflicting findings.

workflow.title: Agree the first useful release
workflow.description: Select a focused offer and customer journey. Document responsibilities, the build sequence, dependencies, budget assumptions, and measurable acceptance criteria.

exampleBuilds.title: Founder launch workspace
exampleBuilds.description: An organized workspace for the customer profile, offer, launch backlog, decisions, and source evidence.

exampleBuilds.title: New market discovery sprint
exampleBuilds.description: A researched segment map and a test plan for a company entering a new region or vertical.

clientInputs: Founder or business owner availability, current offer, target regions, and known customer problems.
Existing customer interviews, sales notes, permitted market evidence, and competitor questions.
Practical constraints: budget, staffing, deadlines, approved claims, and systems already in use.
owner: Business owner with a MoreSpace strategy lead
exitCriteria: The target customer, business problem, offer, and exclusions are documented.
Priority assumptions have evidence, uncertainty notes, and a plan for further testing.
The first release has named owners, a realistic sequence, client inputs, and acceptance checks.
scopeLimits: Company registration, legal entity selection, legal opinions, tax advice, and regulated licensing remain with the client and qualified advisers.
Market research supports decisions; it does not guarantee demand, revenue, investment, or a particular commercial result.

title: Build the brand and digital foundation
summary: Create a consistent identity, a useful website, and the digital journeys a customer needs to understand the company and take the next step.
objective: Launch an accessible, credible digital presence that connects the business offer with clear customer actions and an operating handover.
deliverables: Brand and content system: A practical identity direction, logo applications, color and typography choices, reusable creative templates, and approved message rules.
Website and conversion journeys: A responsive multi-page website or scoped product interface with service detail, clear navigation, conversion paths, structured content, and accessibility checks.
Launch infrastructure: Domain and hosting configuration, environment setup, deployment instructions, access ownership, and recovery steps for the agreed release.
Visibility and measurement setup: A search and answer visibility plan, page metadata, a tracking specification, and validated event implementation where the client has authorized it.

workflow.title: Design the identity and journey
workflow.description: Translate the offer into page architecture, content hierarchy, brand assets, and interactive prototypes. Review messages, accessibility, and the desired next action before implementation.

workflow.title: Build the approved experience
workflow.description: Implement the selected pages or application, integrate approved capture paths, and configure publishing and hosting with client-owned access.

workflow.title: Validate the launch
workflow.description: Check responsive journeys, forms, page metadata, error paths, deployment behavior, permissions, and any authorized events. Deliver a maintenance guide and ownership record.

exampleBuilds.title: Service company launch
exampleBuilds.description: A multi-page company website with service hierarchy, solution blueprints, a project enquiry journey, and a maintainable content structure.

exampleBuilds.title: SaaS launch experience
exampleBuilds.description: A product website and a focused onboarding interface connecting the value proposition with activation steps.

clientInputs: Approved company name, positioning, logo rights, service details, claims, and real proof that may be published.
Client-owned domains, hosting or cloud access, content ownership, required languages, and target devices.
Approved data collection and tracking rules, business contact destinations, and a named content reviewer.
owner: Marketing owner with MoreSpace design and engineering leads
exitCriteria: The agreed page and interaction scope works on representative desktop and mobile journeys.
Contact, onboarding, or purchase actions have a tested destination and a visible failure path.
Publishing access, operating documentation, and the release checklist are handed over to the named owner.
scopeLimits: A domain, website, or social profile does not establish trademark ownership or legal registration.
Rankings, AI answer mentions, accessibility certifications, and conversion improvements are not guaranteed.
Third-party licenses, hosting charges, paid fonts, asset rights, and ongoing maintenance are agreed separately.

title: Create demand and capture enquiries
summary: Connect research, content, paid media, outreach, and landing journeys so attention can become relevant demand.
objective: Give the company a repeatable acquisition process with clear audience rules, reviewed creative, reliable capture, and measures that include lead quality.
deliverables: Audience and channel plan: An ideal customer profile, channel choices, campaign hypotheses, permitted research approach, and an agreed test budget.
Creative and content production: Reviewed campaign assets, social content, search-focused pages, video or voice assets where scoped, and a reusable publishing calendar.
Connected capture and nurture: Landing pages, forms, eligible messaging sequences, source context, and clear qualification and human handoff rules.
Acquisition analysis: A reporting view connecting channel costs, valid leads, qualified demand, and downstream outcomes with consistent definitions.

workflow.title: Choose the audience and offer
workflow.description: Select target segments and a relevant offer. Review source permissions, message claims, exclusions, creative direction, and channel access before activation.

workflow.title: Prepare and release reviewed campaigns
workflow.description: Build the agreed assets and journeys. Validate capture, attribution fields, suppression rules, sending setup, and provider limits before a scoped release.

workflow.title: Improve with sales evidence
workflow.description: Review valid and qualified outcomes with sales, compare like-for-like cohorts, and prioritize the next useful experiment instead of optimizing on clicks alone.

exampleBuilds.title: Connected paid demand funnel
exampleBuilds.description: Reviewed ads and landing pages feeding a CRM queue, with source tracking and qualified lead reporting.

exampleBuilds.title: Research-to-outreach engine
exampleBuilds.description: A permitted account list, reviewed personalization, controlled outreach, response routing, and opportunity feedback.

exampleBuilds.title: Content and visibility operating system
exampleBuilds.description: A research queue, content calendar, approved publishing steps, and search and engagement analysis.

clientInputs: A validated offer, target audience and geography, approved claims, and available sales capacity.
Client-owned ad, analytics, outreach, and website accounts with the required access and paid media budget.
Eligible contact sources, communication permissions, suppression records, and an agreed conversion window.
owner: Marketing lead with a sales qualification owner
exitCriteria: Campaign and capture journeys pass the agreed end-to-end checks.
Every eligible lead has an owner, source context, qualification rule, and next action.
Costs and downstream outcomes can be reconciled for a defined period and population.
scopeLimits: Media spend, sending infrastructure, licensed prospect data, creative production limits, and platform costs are agreed in the scope.
Collection and messaging use permitted sources and approved communication rules; scraped availability does not establish outreach permission.
Lead volume, inbox placement, rankings, revenue, and return on ad spend are not guaranteed.

title: Run sales and onboard customers
summary: Make qualification, follow-up, proposals, opportunity stages, and customer onboarding visible across the team.
objective: Connect an enquiry to an accountable sales process and a documented handoff into delivery, with clear stage criteria and exception handling.
deliverables: CRM and pipeline architecture: A stage model, required fields, qualification rules, record ownership, deduplication rules, and a documented next-action process.
Follow-up and sales coordination: Approved contact workflows, response queues, meeting or task handoffs, proposal preparation inputs, and escalation paths.
Customer onboarding system: A customer intake checklist, agreed requirements, kickoff tasks, access requests, implementation milestones, and delivery owner handoff.
Sales operating scorecard: Defined measures for qualification, response time, pipeline value, conversion, and cycle length, with source records and review cadence.

workflow.title: Define the lifecycle rules
workflow.description: Agree what counts as a valid lead, a qualified opportunity, a won customer, and a delivery-ready handoff. Document time zones, ownership, required evidence, and lost reasons.

workflow.title: Connect approved follow-up
workflow.description: Implement eligible routing and messaging, synchronize selected fields, and keep uncertain replies and failed-provider events in an owner-visible queue.

workflow.title: Hand over the customer
workflow.description: Create onboarding tasks and pass the approved scope, contacts, requirements, and key dates to delivery. Reconcile a sample from enquiry through kickoff before release.

exampleBuilds.title: Lead-to-kickoff workflow
exampleBuilds.description: A qualified CRM opportunity creates a reviewed onboarding checklist, delivery project, responsible owner, and kickoff task.

exampleBuilds.title: Sales follow-up workspace
exampleBuilds.description: An owner-ready queue showing response context, opportunity stage, aging, and the next eligible action.

clientInputs: Sales stages, qualification definitions, sales and delivery owners, current CRM records, and commercial scope templates.
Approved message templates, communication eligibility, time-zone responsibilities, and escalation expectations.
Client access to selected CRM and collaboration accounts and the required provider subscriptions.
owner: Sales owner with a customer onboarding lead
exitCriteria: Duplicate, disqualification, opt-out, reassignment, and failed synchronization paths are tested.
A won opportunity passes scope, context, ownership, and required inputs to delivery without silent data loss.
Sales and delivery agree stage definitions and can review the same source records.
scopeLimits: Proposal and document workflows organize client-approved material; legal contract drafting and approval remain with qualified client advisers.
Payment, e-signature, calendar, telephony, and CRM connections depend on provider access and are separately validated.
The website itself does not operate a live sales inbox or perform outreach without configured accounts and an agreed implementation.

title: Organize the team and deliver the work
summary: Create structured Jira or Asana workspaces and connect Slack or Discord communication with project ownership, delivery updates, and the systems your team actually uses.
objective: Give every project, task, approval, and operational exception a clear owner and place, while keeping communication useful and accessible across locations and time zones.
deliverables: Jira project setup: Selected project configuration, issue types, workflow states, boards, triage queues, permission responsibilities, and reusable delivery templates for the scoped team.
Asana work management setup: Projects, tasks, milestones, ownership, dependencies or rules supported by the selected plan, and reusable onboarding and delivery templates.
Slack workspace structure: A channel map, naming conventions, access ownership, communication guidelines, scoped notification rules, and approved apps or workflow handoffs.

Discord server and community structure: A purposeful server layout, roles and permissions, onboarding guidance, moderation responsibilities, and scoped bot or notification workflows for a team or customer community.
Internal operations tools: A role-aware workspace for selected project, inventory, vendor, or service requests with approval queues, audit context, and exception reporting.
Delivery operating guide: A task and status dictionary, review rhythm, handoff rules, new-member onboarding checklist, and a practical runbook for maintaining the setup.

workflow.title: Map the work and ownership
workflow.description: Review the team structure, current project lifecycle, request types, approval decisions, and communication patterns. Choose a system of record for each item and avoid duplicating the same status across competing tools.

workflow.title: Create the workspaces and channels
workflow.description: Configure scoped project templates, roles, states, channel structure, and onboarding instructions using client-owned admin access. Validate licensing and the exact capabilities available in the selected plan.

workflow.title: Connect useful updates
workflow.description: Connect selected task, CRM, support, or deployment events through permitted APIs and webhooks. Include stable record links, owner context, retries, and a queue for failed or ambiguous events.

workflow.title: Test and hand over operations
workflow.description: Test normal, duplicate, reassignment, access-denied, and failed-provider paths. Train the named administrators and document periodic access review, notification ownership, and recovery actions.

exampleBuilds.title: Client delivery control room
exampleBuilds.description: A CRM handoff creates a reviewed Jira or Asana project from a template and sends a linked update to the approved Slack channel.

exampleBuilds.title: Software release workflow
exampleBuilds.description: A tracked work item links to GitHub implementation and a reviewed release status, with failure and rollback responsibilities visible to the team.

exampleBuilds.title: Employee or contractor onboarding
exampleBuilds.description: A role-specific checklist tracks equipment or access requests, training material, first tasks, and manager confirmation using client-approved policies.

exampleBuilds.title: Customer or developer community
exampleBuilds.description: A Discord server with purposeful channels, member roles, onboarding guidance, escalation routes, and a named moderation team.

exampleBuilds.title: Inventory and vendor workspace
exampleBuilds.description: An internal tool for approved item requests, stock movements, vendor context, fulfillment status, and exception review.

clientInputs: Team structure, project and request types, delivery stages, access roles, and a named administrator for each platform.
Client-owned Jira, Asana, Slack, or Discord access, plan details, approved apps, and the source systems to be connected.
Communication guidelines, internal policies, supported time zones, moderation ownership, and the required handoff expectations.
owner: Operations or delivery lead with client platform administrators
exitCriteria: Selected projects, workflows, channels, roles, and templates match the agreed operating model.
A representative request moves from creation to completion with an owner, status history, and correct handoff.
Notification, permission, duplicate-event, and provider-failure checks pass for the approved integrations.
Administrators can onboard a member, update a template, locate exceptions, and recover a failed handoff using the runbook.
scopeLimits: Jira, Asana, Slack, and Discord are selected to fit the work; the scope does not require using all four or replacing a functioning existing stack.
Workspaces and projects are configured in client-owned accounts. Licenses, app approvals, API access, retention, and available features depend on the selected provider plan.
Ongoing community moderation, employee management, recruitment, HR decisions, security administration, and 24-hour support require a separately defined operating scope.
Automated messages and bots use approved channels and permissions; people remain responsible for important approvals and employment or customer decisions.

title: Support customers and grow the relationship
summary: Connect customer portals, service requests, knowledge, approved messaging, and human escalation so customers know how to get help and teams can follow through.
objective: Make customer onboarding, support, renewal, and community participation coherent, with clear ownership and evidence of the experience after the first sale.
deliverables: Customer service journey: Intake routes, request categories, ownership rules, priority definitions, handoff paths, and the communication expected at each service stage.
Customer portal or request workspace: A scoped account or request experience with appropriate roles, status visibility, required inputs, and a tested path for corrections or support.
Knowledge and assisted response system: An approved knowledge base, retrieval and citation rules, reviewed response patterns, and human escalation for uncertain or sensitive questions.
Retention and community workflow: Eligible onboarding and follow-up messages, feedback collection, renewal tasks, community structure where relevant, and a customer outcome review process.

workflow.title: Map customer expectations
workflow.description: Review customer questions, commitments, service windows, request ownership, and available support capacity. Agree which responses require a person and how customers reach that person.

workflow.title: Build the service routes
workflow.description: Create the scoped portal, queues, knowledge structure, and approved messaging paths. Validate customer identity, record permissions, retention, and service handoffs before activation.

workflow.title: Evaluate the experience
workflow.description: Test customer and agent journeys, failed or uncertain responses, and escalation continuity. Review response quality, lifecycle cohorts, and feedback with the customer success owner.

exampleBuilds.title: Customer portal and request tracker
exampleBuilds.description: An authenticated portal where customers can share required inputs, view the scoped service status, and raise a request.

exampleBuilds.title: Knowledge assistant with escalation
exampleBuilds.description: A source-grounded assistant for approved questions with explicit uncertainty behavior and context passed to a human queue.

exampleBuilds.title: Renewal and feedback workflow
exampleBuilds.description: Scheduled owner tasks and eligible customer messages that connect feedback, renewal context, and actual lifecycle outcomes.

clientInputs: Customer service commitments, support hours, escalation owners, renewal rules, and approved communication channels.
An approved knowledge collection with ownership, update responsibilities, visibility rules, and source quality review.
Customer account model, data retention rules, permission requirements, and representative support examples for evaluation.
owner: Customer success lead with support and knowledge owners
exitCriteria: Customers can submit the agreed request and follow its next step with appropriate permissions.
The support owner receives the necessary context and can resolve or escalate the request.
Knowledge responses meet the agreed evaluation criteria, cite the permitted source where required, and hand uncertain cases to a person.
Retention reporting uses defined cohorts and separates customer churn from revenue changes.
scopeLimits: A chatbot or knowledge assistant is not a substitute for a qualified professional or a promise of autonomous customer resolution.
Staffed support, call centers, community moderation, response commitments, and languages are specified separately.
Customer communication is activated only with approved eligibility, account setup, content, and responsible owners.

title: See the performance of the whole company
summary: Bring sales, delivery, acquisition, customer, and management data into a common reporting system with transparent definitions and reliable refresh.
objective: Give leaders a dependable view of how the company is performing and where an action is needed, while keeping commercial assumptions and data limitations visible.
deliverables: Management metric dictionary: Definitions, formulas, units, cohorts, cost boundaries, reporting windows, and named owners for the agreed operating and financial measures.
Data foundations and reporting model: Source mapping, stable identifiers, transformations, refresh rules, reconciliation checks, and documented exceptions.
Executive and team dashboards: Role-relevant views of acquisition, sales pipeline, delivery, customer health, and scoped commercial reporting with useful filters and source context.
Review and action rhythm: A weekly or monthly review structure with diagnostic questions, decision records, owner tasks, and a process for correcting inaccurate inputs.

workflow.title: Define the business questions
workflow.description: Agree the decisions the report should support. Define revenue, recurring revenue where relevant, customer counts, costs, and time windows with the client finance and business owners.

workflow.title: Connect and reconcile the data
workflow.description: Use authorized sources and provider APIs to bring agreed fields into a maintainable model. Validate currency, time zones, duplicates, refunds, lifecycle states, freshness, and representative totals.

workflow.title: Publish actionable views
workflow.description: Create owner-specific dashboards and exceptions, document formulas, and test the views against source records. Review actual decisions and prioritize the next data quality improvement.

exampleBuilds.title: Company performance cockpit
exampleBuilds.description: A management dashboard connecting marketing cost, qualified pipeline, delivery exceptions, customer cohorts, and defined commercial outcomes.

exampleBuilds.title: Operational reconciliation queue
exampleBuilds.description: An internal view that identifies unmatched records, missing fields, stale sources, and owner actions before a report is trusted.

exampleBuilds.title: Invoice or billing operations workspace
exampleBuilds.description: A scoped interface for preparing client-approved billing records, tracking status, and reconciling source events with the finance owner.

clientInputs: Business questions, metric owners, finance-approved definitions, cost boundaries, and reporting cadence.
Authorized source access, data dictionaries, stable record identifiers, currency and time-zone rules, and representative source records.
Access policy, dashboard audience, required refresh intervals, and a named owner for source corrections.
owner: Business or finance reporting owner with a MoreSpace data lead
exitCriteria: Every published measure has a visible definition, population, window, source, and accountable owner.
Representative totals reconcile to the approved sources or have explained and owned exceptions.
Refresh failures, incomplete inputs, and stale data are visible rather than silently presented as current.
The intended audience can find the relevant decision and trace the important values to source evidence.
scopeLimits: Management reporting and finance workflow software do not provide statutory accounting, audited statements, tax filing, financial advice, or certification.
Source systems and client finance owners remain authoritative for accounting policy, tax treatment, and payment decisions.
Forecasts and ROI scenarios are assumptions-based planning outputs; the scope states the data, uncertainty, and calculation limits.

title: Scale with useful software, automation, and AI
summary: Improve what works, remove repeatable friction, and expand the company through tested software, bounded AI, stronger data, and a clear operating rhythm.
objective: Turn observed bottlenecks into prioritized improvements that the team can maintain, with measurable value and a realistic human oversight model.
deliverables: Improvement and automation roadmap: A prioritized backlog based on task volume, elapsed time, failure cost, customer impact, feasibility, and the evidence available.
Scoped software or AI implementation: A focused product increment, internal tool, workflow, research agent, or knowledge assistant with explicit inputs, outputs, permissions, and review points.
Evaluation and release plan: Representative examples, quality and failure checks, cost measurement, staged release criteria, recovery steps, and a named decision owner.
Operating handover and iteration: Runbooks, access ownership, exception queues, provider usage visibility, review cadence, and a prioritized next release.

workflow.title: Choose the bottleneck that matters
workflow.description: Observe the current workflow, sample real records, define the useful outcome, and estimate the effort before selecting a tool. Keep the baseline and proposed benefit separate.

workflow.title: Design bounded assistance
workflow.description: Choose deterministic rules, software, or AI according to the task. Specify approved sources, least-required permissions, uncertain-output behavior, cost boundaries, and human decisions.

workflow.title: Evaluate and release in stages
workflow.description: Use representative cases and failure scenarios to compare quality, completion, cost, and time with the baseline. Release the selected scope with monitoring, owner-visible exceptions, and recovery instructions.

workflow.title: Improve from real operation
workflow.description: Review how the system is used, diagnose recurring failures, update approved knowledge and rules, and prioritize the next change with the accountable business owner.

exampleBuilds.title: Research agent with a reviewed output queue
exampleBuilds.description: Permitted data collection and evidence summarization produce structured records for expert review before operational use.

exampleBuilds.title: Cross-team exception routing
exampleBuilds.description: A failed data or service event creates a linked work item, notifies its owner, and records the eventual resolution.

exampleBuilds.title: Internal product expansion
exampleBuilds.description: A focused role-aware module connects customer, project, inventory, or management records with an existing operating model.

exampleBuilds.title: International operating rollout
exampleBuilds.description: A scoped adaptation of approved content, currency displays, time-zone handoffs, local data requirements, and support ownership for an additional market.

clientInputs: A named business owner, current process evidence, representative normal and failure examples, and the intended improvement.
Approved provider and data access, representative evaluation data, risk and permission boundaries, and a realistic operating budget.
Deployment ownership, support responsibilities, acceptance criteria, recovery expectations, and the team available to maintain the system.
owner: Business process owner with MoreSpace engineering and AI leads
exitCriteria: The agreed outcome, evaluation set, quality threshold, cost boundary, and human handoff are documented.
Representative tasks and failure paths pass the agreed checks with source evidence and owner-visible exceptions.
The client can operate, monitor, update, and recover the release using the handover material.
The next improvement is selected from actual operating evidence rather than unverified automation promises.
scopeLimits: Automation and AI operate within a defined task and permission scope; they do not autonomously run the entire company or replace accountable business decisions.
Model quality, provider availability, rate limits, usage costs, and source changes require ongoing review.
International legal, employment, tax, data-transfer, and regulated-market requirements are assessed by the client and qualified advisers; implementation follows the approved requirements.
Ongoing maintenance, additional markets, continuous evaluation, and managed operations are agreed as a separate service scope.
